plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-12 from the official Southern Utah University 2026-2027 General Catalog (current edition, catoid=28) Cybersecurity program page and its linked official degree map workbook, 'Cybersecurity Degree Maps (2026-2027)', 'Cybersecurity (Campus)' tab, last updated/reviewed July 27, 2026. The workbook's Index lists an Online degree map as 'N/A'; this is the campus plan. Semester placement is the university's official sample 4-year campus academic plan (SUU Program Maps, 2026-2027), which the source itself labels a guide only; students confirm specifics in Degree Works with a Student Success Advisor. This is a BS-only program: the catalog page prints no BA total-credits line and the degree map carries no foreign-language note. The catalog's BS requirement is 12 credits of Math or Science courses (at least 3 credits MATH numbered 1000 or above, excluding MATH 1030 or MATH 1040, and at least 3 credits of Science courses numbered 1000 or above), and the catalog notes a portion of the BS requirement may be met by satisfying General Education requirements; the map does not label BS courses separately. The catalog's General Education block prints only Core Course Requirements (12+ credits) and Breadth Area Requirements (16+ credits) with 'See General Education for course options'; the map's GE rows are recorded as printed. The catalog's Free Electives section prints no fixed figure (the total is determined by the General Education courses taken, degree type, additional credits earned and prerequisite courses needed). Every term's courses sum to the map's printed term total (16/16/15/15/15/15/15/13) and the plan to the catalog's printed BS degree total of 120. The catalog's curriculum reconciles: Mathematics Requirements 6-8 + CSCY Common Core 15 + Cybersecurity Core Requirements 48 + Cybersecurity Major Electives 9 + Cybersecurity Electives 3 = the printed Curriculum heading of 81-83 credits. All five Common Core courses and all fifteen named Cybersecurity Core courses appear on the map. The map exercises the catalog's choices, recorded as printed and disclosed here: MATH 1190 - Introduction to Data Science for the first Mathematics 'Complete One of the Following' group (MATH 1031 - Statistical Reasoning 3, MATH 1040 - Statistical Inference 4, MATH 1190 3) and MATH 1050 - College Algebra for the second group (MATH 1050 4, MATH 1060 - Trigonometry 3), so the map's mathematics total is 7 credits, inside the catalog's 6-8 range; and COMM 1010 - Introduction to Communication for the Cybersecurity Core's 'Complete One of the Following' communication choice (COMM 1010, COMM 2110, COMM 2120, each 3 credits). The map's three generic major upper-division elective slots total exactly the Major Electives block's 9 credits and its one generic CSCY elective slot the Cybersecurity Electives block's 3 credits. The map's Free Electives rows total 22 credits; the catalog prints no free-elective total, so that figure is the map's as printed. Catalog titles are recorded where the map shortens them (CSCY 2400 Technology and Ethics, CYBR 2500 Data Communications and Networking, CSCY 1200 Critical Thinking for Logic and Design). Program information printed in the catalog: all courses must be passed with a C- (1.7) or better to be counted in the major; credits older than 10 years must be approved by the CSCY Department Chair; students who complete this degree have also completed the requirements for the Information Technology (AAS) and can also earn the Computer Science (Minor); CSCY 1000 - Introduction to Computer Applications and the Internet is suggested for students without computer application skills but does not pertain to the degree, and is not placed in this plan.
